regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Stowe leads with 17" over the week, with the biggest day Friday at 9". Light snow is expected Thursday through Saturday, with northwest wind gusting to 23 mph Saturday. Killington also totals 17", peaking Friday at 9" with north wind gusting to 26 mph. Jay Peak has 11".

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Kirkwood leads with 18", with 16" falling Friday, and Palisades and Sugar Bowl each total 15" with 13" on Friday. Friday brings a chance of thunderstorms and a change to rain before snow returns Friday night. Snow continues through Sunday night.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Whistler totals 28", with 13" on Tuesday, and then rain dominates. Wednesday brings rain at times heavy, with southeast wind gusting to 60 km/h in the morning. Snow returns Sunday, with 11" expected.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: Mammoth totals 9", all falling Friday. Strong southwest wind gusts to 60 mph Friday night and remains gusty through Sunday, so expect difficult lift and visibility conditions. Snow continues Sunday night.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Crystal Mountain totals 6", with the biggest day Sunday at 4", and Stevens Pass also gets 6", all on Sunday. Rain and snow mix Friday through Sunday, with snow levels near pass elevation. Mt. Baker totals 5", peaking Sunday at 3".

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center says a second, colder storm could bring snow to the Sierra and northern California ranges around Monday Nov 16, with moderate accumulations possible. Confidence is moderate, given that model timing and amounts still differ.
